commenti.body:
Yeah, I think this is my favorite Jim Jarmusch movie that I have seen. I only saw it once, some years ago, so my comments are my recollection and I could be forgetting things- But I agree with you, I didn't think that Farehani's character was meant to be taken as worse or bad. Just different. I remember thinking their relationship was wholesome and relatively drama-free.

This movie is an interesting experiment in how little conflict you can have in a story and still make it an interesting movie. From what I recall, not much really "happens" in this movie in the sense of an obstacle or conflict to overcome (not until >!the dog eats his poem book)!<. It's basically a slice of life movie about a guy who drives a bus, writes poem, walks his dog, goes around the neighborhood pub, loves and supports his wife even though they're very different.

I find it fascinating, and I keep thinking about it, and that's what makes it a great movie, to me.

>People seem to take issue with Farehani's character being painted as frivolous

I didn't love the character. I'm not sold on your take.

But I appreciated how Driver was able to communicate his character's love/appreciation for her despite her frivolity. And it occurred to me that maybe there was more there that we don't see because we spend so little time with her. So I let it go.
